text:
The Islanders come in with points in five straight (3-0-2), though the last one stung: a 3-2 overtime loss to LAK on Thursday, when Brandt Clarke won it despite Darcy Kuemper's 41 saves. They're playing without Calum Ritchie and Matias Maccelli, and Simon Holmstrom has moved onto the first power-play unit and is up to 20:31 a night from 15:43. The Stars have won four straight, the latest an overtime win over WPG in which Jason Robertson reached 500 career points, though Oskar Bäck, Esa Lindell and Sam Steel are out.

The teams look close at five on five, each with 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances taken). Our model still leans Dallas, 3.06 to 2.61 in expected goals tonight. The special-teams matchup to watch: DAL's power play creates 0.78 expected goals a game, and NYI's penalty kill allows 0.94 while the Islanders take 4.6 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Ilya Sorokin and Jake Oettinger are both well above expected, +8.8 and +10.4 in goals saved above expected (saves beyond what the shots should allow). Sorokin was +22.3 last season; Oettinger was +2.2.

For the Islanders, we like Bo Horvat, with a 36% chance to score and a power-play role. Matthew Schaefer, the 2025 first overall pick, gets 55% for a point. For Dallas, Wyatt Johnston is at 38% to score, Robertson 37%, and Mikko Rantanen, on a four-game point streak, has a 74% chance of a point.
